title: Conformer: Convolution-augmented Transformer for Speech Recognition
grouping: No container: the module is one row of eight boxes, with a single black arrow leaving the input line, arching over the whole row and coming down into the residual adder at the right end. Grouping is by colour family only - boxes of the same layer kind share a fill.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles (small radius), equal size, pastel fills with a slightly darker outline of the same hue: pale yellow for the normalisations (Layernorm, BatchNorm), peach for both Pointwise Conv boxes, light grey for the activations (Glu, Swish), lilac for 1D Depthwise Conv, pale green for Dropout. Short black arrows join them; the sum is a small light-blue circle with a plus. Black sans labels, two lines where needed; no tensor shapes.
proposed_highlight: Nothing is emphasised: the module is shown as a plain layer list, and the depthwise convolution differs only by its unique lilac fill.
lesson: In a one-row module, colour boxes by layer kind (norms one tint, pointwise convs another, activations grey) so repeated kinds match at a glance, and draw the residual as one arc over the whole row into a circled plus.
notes: Venue written as arXiv: the arXiv comment says 'Submitted to Interspeech 2020' (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref), which does not confirm acceptance; remembered as Interspeech 2020. year = arXiv preprint year (2005.08100).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: convolution module of the Conformer ASR block

core.what: one horizontal chain of eight layer boxes (Layernorm -> Pointwise Conv -> Glu Activation -> 1D Depthwise Conv -> BatchNorm -> Swish Activation -> Pointwise Conv -> Dropout) ending in a + node, with a residual line looping over the top from the input to that node

relations.form: eight equal rounded boxes on one line, joined by short straight arrows
a residual line rises before the first box, runs along the top of the whole chain and drops into the blue + circle at the right end

channels.colour: fill = layer type: yellow = normalisation, orange = pointwise convolution, grey = activation, purple = depthwise convolution, green = dropout, blue = the residual add; repeated types repeat their fill
channels.line: solid arrows only, all data flow

quality.strengths: The block is a single straight chain with short aligned arrows, the residual is one line over the top, and repeated layer types (two pointwise convs) share a fill so the sandwich around the depthwise convolution is visible.
quality.weaknesses: Nothing is drawn as data (no tensor shapes or channel counts), so the expansion by the pointwise conv and the gating halving by GLU are invisible; the depthwise convolution, the module's point, is the same size as Dropout; the colour code is not keyed.

insights.structure: One horizontal chain of eight rounded boxes (Layernorm, Pointwise Conv, Glu Activation, 1D Depthwise Conv, BatchNorm, Swish Activation, Pointwise Conv, Dropout) ending in a circled '+'.
insights.data: No data drawn; only operation names inside boxes.
insights.emphasis: Box fill encodes operation type (yellow norms, orange pointwise convs, grey activations, purple depthwise conv, green dropout); the depthwise conv is the only purple box.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with short arrows; a residual line leaves before Layernorm, runs over the top and drops into the '+' at the far right.
insights.avoid: Colour code has no legend, and the long single row is very wide and short, hard to fit in a column.

arrangement.units: one unframed chain of module boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare arrow entering from the left
